title: Simplified production and concentration of lentiviral vectors to achieve high transduction in primary human T cells
markdown:
## Protocol: I have donor-derived human CD4-positive, CD45RA-positive T cells and a lentiviral vector carrying a detectable expression marker. I need a workflow to stimulate the cells, introduce the vector, maintain them after transduction, and use flow cytometry to quantify marker-positive cells. Focus on the primary T-cell experiment rather than making the vector stock.

### Overview

This protocol outlines the workflow for stimulating donor-derived human CD4-positive, CD45RA-positive T cells, transducing them with a lentiviral vector carrying a detectable expression marker, maintaining the cells post-transduction, and quantifying marker-positive cells via flow cytometry. The procedure focuses on the primary T-cell experiment steps, assuming the lentiviral vector stock is available.

### Materials/Reagents

Donor-derived human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) or peripheral blood lymphocytes (PBLs); Negative bead isolation kits (Miltenyi) for CD4+CD45RA+ cell isolation; X-VIVO 15 medium (Lonza); Fetal calf serum (FCS, Gibco) or Human serum (Biosera); Recombinant human IL-2 and IL-7; Anti-CD3 antibodies (OKT3, Insight Biotechnology) and soluble anti-CD28 antibodies (BD Pharmingen), or anti-CD3/CD28 activation beads (Invitrogen); Lentiviral vector stock; Polybrene (Sigma); PBS; RPMI 1640 growth medium; APC-conjugated anti-CD271 (NGFR) antibody (BD Pharmingen).

### Equipment

Ficoll-Hypaque reagent; Centrifuge capable of Ficoll separation and elutriation; Cell culture flasks/incubators (37°C, 5% CO2); Sterile 2 mL pipettes; Vortex mixer; Millex-HV filters (0.45 μm pore PVDF, Millipore); Sorval Discovery 100 SE centrifuge with AH-629 rotor; Polycarbonate/polyallomer conical tubes (Beckman); Flow cytometer.

### Safety & Sterility

Maintain sterile technique throughout all cell culture and transduction steps. Use appropriate biosafety precautions when handling human-derived cells and viral vectors. Ensure all media and reagents are sterile.

## Reagent Preparation

### Pre-transfection

1. The precipitate was formed by adding 80 μg of DNA to a final volume of 1.35 mL distilled H2O and 150 μl 2.5M CaCl2 (Sigma). A sterile 2 mL pipette was used to bubble air through the DNA mix, during which, 1.5 mL 2x HEPES-buffered saline (280 mM NaCl, 50 mM HEPES, 1.5 mM Na2HPO4, pH 7.0) was added dropwise into the precipitate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. The solution was briefly vortexed and incubated at room temperature for 30 min. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->
3. Following this, the solution was mixed again by gentle vortexing, and then added dropwise to the cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S03 -->

## Lentivirus Production

### Day 0: Transfection

1. HEK 293T/17 cells (ATCC No. CRL-11268) were cultured in high glucose-containing Dulbecco’s modified Eagle’s medium (DMEM; Lonza) supplemented with 10% foetal calf serum (FCS, Gibco) at 37°C at 5% CO2, unless otherwise stated. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
2. Flasks were rocked gently in a circular motion to distribute the precipitates, and then returned to the incubator at 3% CO2 unless otherwise stated. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
3. Four to six hrs later, cells were gently washed once with PBS and fresh growth medium added. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->
4. Sixteen hrs post-transfection, the medium was replaced with RPMI supplemented with 5% FCS unless otherwise stated and incubated at 5% CO2 for 24 hrs prior to the initial collection. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S04 -->
5. Sodium butyrate (Sigma) was added 16 hr post-transfection into the culture medium at a final concentration of 1 mM. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S05 -->

### Day 1-2: Harvest

1. A second collection was made after a further 24 hrs. The conditioned medium from the two harvests was combined and cleared by centrifugation at 1500 rpm for 5 min at 4°C then passed through a 0.45 μm pore PVDF Millex-HV filter (Millipore). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S01 -->

## Lentivirus Concentration

### Post-Harvest Concentration

1. Concentration of lentivirus using ultracentrifugation was performed with a Sorval Discovery 100 SE centrifuge using an AH-629 rotor. 30 mL of filtered lentivirus supernatant was added to 36 mL pollyallomer conical tubes (Beckman). Centrifugation was performed for 90 min at 20,000 g. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S01 -->
2. Supernatant was completely removed and virus pellets resuspended in 300 μL PBS overnight at 4°C and stored at -80°C until use. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B03-T0-S02 -->

## Primary T Cell Isolation and Stimulation

### Isolation

1. Isolate human peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) from healthy volunteers or blood donations using Ficoll-Hypaque density gradient centrifugation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S01 -->
2. Alternatively, isolate peripheral blood lymphocytes (PBLs) from PBMCs using centrifugal elutriation. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S02 -->
3. Isolate CD4-positive, CD45RA-positive T cells from the PBL fraction using negative bead isolation kits (e.g., Miltenyi). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S03 -->

### Stimulation and Culture

1. Culture the isolated CD4+CD45RA+ T cells in X-VIVO 15 medium supplemented with either 5% fetal calf serum (FCS) or 5% human serum, along with interleukin-2 (IL-2) at 100 ng/mL and interleukin-7 (IL-7) at 15 ng/mL. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S01 -->
2. Stimulate the cultured lymphocytes using one of the following methods: (1) plate-bound anti-CD3 (OKT3) combined with soluble anti-CD28, or (2) anti-CD3/CD28 activation beads. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S02 -->

## Lentiviral Transduction

### Transduction Setup

1. Prepare the lentiviral transduction mix by adding lentivirus to the stimulated primary CD45RA+ lymphocytes cultured in X-VIVO media supplemented with 10% FCS (initial conditions) or 10% human serum (optimal conditions) and polybrene at a final concentration of 6 μg/mL. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S01 -->
2. Add the lentivirus to achieve a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 50. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S02 -->
3. Incubate the cells overnight with the virus. After incubation, remove the lentivirus-containing medium and replace it with fresh culture medium. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S03 -->
4. Continue cell culture for 48 hours under initial conditions or 24 hours under optimal conditions. Harvest the cells and analyze the percentage of marker-positive cells (NGFR+) by flow cytometry using an APC-conjugated anti-CD271 antibody. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S04 -->

## Titration and Analysis

### Titration

1. Titres were determined by transducing 1 × 105 Jurkat cells in 100 μl of RPMI 1640 growth medium. Titres were determined in triplicate with serial dilutions from 1:10 to 1:1000 for un-concentrated vector stocks, or from 1:100 to 1:10000 for concentrated vector stocks in a final volume of 100 μl with 6 μg/mL polybrene (Sigma). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S01 -->
2. The following day, plates were spun at 1,500 rpm for 5 min to remove cells from suspension and fresh growth medium added. After a further 48 hr incubation, cells were harvested and NGFR expression was determined by flow cytometry using APC-CD271 antibody (BD Pharmingen). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S02 -->

## References

- [1] Simplified production and concentration of lentiviral vectors to achieve high transduction in primary human T cells — https://doi.org/10.1186/1472-6750-13-98
